Title: What is the difference between Personal and Enterprise License?
Content: There is a distinction based on the user's status. All users must comply with the "Terms of Service." Freelancers are allowed to use personal licenses, but all other companies (studios, game companies, research companies, etc.) must purchase enterprise licenses. If a corporate entity purchases personal licenses, access to the purchased Marvelous Designer license may be restricted or terminated without prior notice. If a personal license is purchased using a company's credit card or company email address, it may be considered as a purchase by a corporate customer.

Title: Retopology (ver. 12)
Content: Objective Allow the user to draw topology lines onto existing patterns creating a new mesh with a lower polygon count and edge-loops optimized for animation. Create Topology Location 3D/2D Window Tool Bart Topology Tools Operation Follow the path indicated in Location above. When a Topology tool selected, patterns will be displayed as transparent. When you place the mouse cursor over a pattern, the pattern is highlighted in its original color. New topology can only be created on one pattern at a time. Click on the highlighted pattern to add a topology point. Topology can be created in both the 2D and 3D Windows, though we recommend using the 2D Window primarily. Creating Face When creating Topology lines, a Topology face is created if a closed shape is drawn. Topology faces are created only on shapes with 3 or 4 points/sides. To stop drawing Topology before closing a shape (leaving an open shape), double-click to finish. Cancel point creation Cancel points one-by-one by pressing Delete/Backspace Key on the keyboard. Cancel all points: Press ESC, Ctl + Z Key on the keyboard. Add Division Loop While hovering over an edge with the Create Topology Tool, press Shift + Ctrl and click to add an edge loop across continuous faces. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Cut Topology Faces Existing blue topology faces can be split by drawing new Topology Points/Edges across them. If cut faces result in Ngons, any blue topology faces with more than 4 sides will be highlighted in orange. Edit Topology Location 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar Edit Topology Tool Operation Follow the path indicated in the Location above. Existing topology is highlighted in sky blue after selecting the Edit Topology Tool and Place the mouse cursor over a pattern with existing topology. Select a Topology point, line, or face, and edit it by holding and moving it, or deleting it with the Delete Key. Point/ Line / Face multi-selection While holding the Shift or the Ctrl Key, click on multiple topology points/lines one at a time to add them to a selection. 2D point drag selection While pressing Ctrl key on the keyboard and drag to select multiple topology points. Line loop selection Double click a topology line to loop select. Delete Point/ Line/ Face Press Delete key on the keyboard or right-click and select the delete menu to delete Point/ Line/ Face. Extrude Select lines, press Shift + Ctrl and drag to Extrude. Right-click popup menu Right-click on a point, line, face, pattern or background to access the popup menus. The menu that appears may vary depending on what is applied. Delete Delete selected object. Show Topology Only (3D) Display only the topology, excluding garments or other objects. Show All Unhide everything in the scene in 3D window. Merge Merge two or more points. Merge All Merge all topology points by distance. Set the distance between topology points and click the apply button to merge. Click the close button to close the dialog. Add Division (Current Pattern) Add division on a selected pattern. Adds one division level at a time. Add All Division Add division to entire Topology face. (right-click on the background to pop-up this menu) Remesh (duplicate) Convert (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (duplicate) Convert All (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face of the entire pattern. Remesh (replace) Convert (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) Delete an existing pattern and create a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (replace) Convert All (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) Delete the entire pattern and create new mesh based on created topology face. Show/ Hide Show/ Hide created Topology from 3D Main menu Display 3D garment Show topology. Topology Ghost Display/Snapping Based on The Sewing Lines (Above Ver.11) When Topology Points meet pattern edges with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. These ghost Topology Points help you snap any new topology you create across sewing relationships to exactly the same place as the existing topology on patterns across the seam. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Topology Ghost Display/Snapping across Sewing Relationships for Internal Lines When Topology Points meet Internal Lines with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. Drag Select Topology Points Click outside of an area of blue topology and drag across it to select multiple Topology Points at once. Click and hold the 'Shift' Key, then click and drag over an additional area of blue topology to add Topology Points to an existing selection. Drag Deselect Topology Points Click and hold the 'Control' Key, then click and drag over an existing selection of Topology Points to remove Topology Points from that selection. Patch Topology Location 2D Window Tool Bar Patch Topology Tool Operation (Above Ver.11) Navigate to the interface/menu Location above. Select the 'Patch Topology' Tool, and a pop-up box will appear where you can adjust the number of subdivisions for an edge. Subdivisions Adjust the number of edge subdivisions Create After the patch shape is closed, click the 'Create' button, and the patch lines will turn into topology faces. Clear Delete all in-progress patch lines. Create patch lines on a 2D pattern. Internal topology will appear divided into the preset number of subdivisions along edges, if a a closed patch section is either triangular or rectangular. You can change the number of subdivisions for the next edge while a Topology Patch is in progress (before the patch shape is closed). You can also change the number of subdivisions after closing a patch section (but before clicking 'Create') by selecting the completed patch edge and changing the number in the 'Subdivisions' field. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Snap Patch Topology to Internal Shapes/Lines Patch Topology edges will snap to both external and internal pattern lines and curve points. Snap Patch Topology to Convex Curves Patch Topology edges will now snap to both concave and convex curves. If the curvature of an edge is too extreme for a patch to be created, add one or several curve points along the curved edge with the 'Add Point/Split Line' tool to divide the curve into sections with less extreme curvature. Evaluate Patch Validity at Creation After closing a Topology Patch and clicking 'Create', if the drawn patch would create overlapping geometry, an error window pop-up will be raised - return to the Patch Topology tool and update the patch as necessary to avoid overlapping edges/vertices. If the drawn patch would not result in overlapping geometry, the Topology Patch will be created and displayed in blue. Note: The algorithm for patch topology has been improved, resulting in a more efficient mesh. (ver. 2024.0)

Title: Account Integration FAQ User Guide (CLO-SET account)
Content: Objective Access all CLO Virtual Fashion services using a single email account. This FAQ will cover the updates and changes to login methods for Marvelous Designer Personal &amp Student license account types. This change will NOT affect Enterprise &amp Academic account types at this time. Please check the general FAQ if you have questions about the account merging process (CLO-SET accounts). Details 1) Change in sign in method Effective date on the release of Marvelous Designer 2024.0. What does this cover? Marvelous Designer website / Software version 2024.0 and above. Software Version (12,11,10 and below) Software Version Above 2024.0 How to login Existing User ID &amp Password CLO-SET Account &amp Password 2) How do I get a CLO-SET Account &amp Password if I have an existing Marvelous Designer ID? Check out our detailed step-by-step guide HERE. 3) What is the difference between a CLO-SET account and my previous Marvelous Designer ID? With your old Marvelous Designer ID you had to have multiple logins to access all of the CLO Virtual Fashion (CVF) products and services. Now with one CLO-SET account you can access all CLO Virtual Fashion services without additional logins. 4) I am using a perpetual license for Marvelous Designer. Do I have to merge my account? You do not have to If you are only logging into Marvelous Designer software only. If you want to access the Marvelous Designer website, you will need to follow the on screen prompt to merge your account into a CLO-SET account. Or you can check out our detailed step-by-step guide HERE. 5) Can I still use my Perpetual License after I merge my account with CLO-SET? Yes! All data/assets/subscription information associated with your pre-existing account will remain the same. You can download your software licenses from the same location, in My Account page. 6) How do I login to CLO / Marvelous Designer / Jinny after I merge my account? You can login to CLO / Marvelous Designer / Jinny with your CLO-SET Account &amp Password. 7) I have a subscription license for Marvelous Designer and I like to use an older version than 2024.0. Do I have to use a different sign in or can I use the CLO-SET account? If you have an old installer on your device and you have access to versions below 12: Use the older login method. Login to the installed version you wish to use with your User ID &amp Password (same as before). For 2024.0 and above: you can log in to all CLO Virtual Fashion product (CLO/Marvelous Designer/CONNECT/CLO-SET) websites and software with your CLO-SET account. 8) I bought items from the Marvelous Designer Store (before CONNECT existed). Where can I download my purchased items? All items purchased from the Marvelous Designer Store will be downloadable from CONNECT's My Page &gt Purchase tab. *This applies to purchases made after April 28, 2020 on the Marvelous Designer store page. If you have purchases made before April 28, 2020, those are still stored and downloadable from the Marvelous Designer &gt My Account page. 9) I have both CLO and Marvelous Designer IDs and I use them frequently. How does it affect me? You no longer have to use two separate logins! You can continue using your licenses without functional change for both CLO and Marvelous Designer. All you have to do is sign in with your CLO-SET account. You can check the license information for your products on the CLO or Marvelous Designer websites. 10) I like to use different email addresses for CLO and Marvelous Designer for my own reasons and want to keep them separate. Can I still have separate accounts? Yes, make sure to use the different email addresses for your CLO-SET merge so that you will have two separate CLO-SET accounts. The accounts are tied to each email address and the licenses associated with each account will be included in that merge. If you wish to unify your email addresses in the future or have other questions, please contact our support team at support@clo-set.com or submit a request. 11) I am using my software in an offline environment. Does this change affect me? Your access to your software will remain unaffected, you can continue using your pre-existing account user ID &amp password without change. If you choose to sign in to the websites for any of the CLO Virtual Fashion (CVF) products and services you will be prompted to merge your account into a CLO-SET account. Check out our detailed step-by-step guide HERE. 12) How do I change my password after I merge my accounts into a CLO-SET account? When you click 'Change Password' on the Marvelous Designer website or any CLO Virtual Fashion (CVF) product page, you will be redirected to the CLO-SET My Page, where you can change your password. If you are already on the CLO-SET website, you can change the password under the settings tab on My page. * If you are using a version of the software below 2024.0, your password for the software will not be synchronized with CLO-SET account. **See Question 13 if you want to change your password for an older version. 13) I'm using a version of Marvelous Designer that is below 2024.0 (Version 12,11,10, 9, etc). How do I change my password for my software login? If you have integrated into the CLO-SET account: contact us via the Marvelous Designer support team. If you dont have an integrated CLO-SET account: reset your password via the password reset page. 14) What happens to my subscription cycle if I change my account email? Changing your account email will NOT impact your subscription cycle or payment information. Please note that the email notifications on the renewal and payment confirmation will be sent to your original email registered at the point of subscription. If you need assistance regarding accounts merging or have questions, please contact us at support@clo-set.com or submit a request, and our support team will promptly respond to your inquiry.

Title: How to Prevent Marvelous Designer File Corruption
Content: Objective This article describes why Marvelous Designer project file .zprj and garment file .zpac are corrupted and how to prevent them. Failed to read the Project file: Unzip error~ Problem Situations When launching Marvelous Designer, get an error saying failed to read the project file. When opening a project file saved on the computer, it says it is unreadable. When trying to save the file, it says it can't be saved. Opening the file takes a long time and eventually fails. Causes and Solutions Case 1. Disk Full... Actually If disk space is insufficient during the process of designing and saving garments in Marvelous Designer, file corruption may actually occur. So make sure you have enough free space on your PC's drive. We recommend that you have at least 20GB of free space to install and run Marvelous Designer. You can make free space by deleting or backing up unnecessary files. See also: Marvelous Designer System Requirements Case 2. Mechanical Malfunction and/or Connection Failure File corruption may occur due to physical failure, disk error, or poor connection. You can check disk status through the built-in disk management app or disk management utility on Windows and macOS. In case of physical failure, contact your company's IT support department or the place of purchase. Case 3. No Permission to File Read and Write All computer operating systems, including Windows and macOS, have permission to read/write your files. If you do not have or only have partial permissions to read/write, Marvelous Designer file corruption may occur. The following post explains how to gain read/write permissions for Marvelous Designer files on Windows and macOS. Disk access rights required when Marvelous Designer running If you are a corporate customer, please contact your company's IT/Security department. Case 4. Blocking File Read and Write, or Data Tampering by Security Apps Certain security programs, such as antivirus and Internet communication monitoring tools, may restrict Internet access and file creation of software such as Marvelous Designer. In their detailed settings, change the Marvelous Designer Internet access and file read/write settings to "Allow". In the case of enterprise companies, they often use stronger security solutions than those described above, and in some cases, the files themselves created by Marvelous Designer are tampered with. For corporate users, please contact your IT/Security department. Case 5. Two or More Marvelous Designer Running Simultaneously If you use two or more Marvelous Designer at the same time, there is a possibility that the internal data of the Marvelous Designer project file may be lost or corrupted. All you know that it's a good way to save file often. And if you need to save the final result, save it with only one Marvelous Designer running. Case 6. External Storage Connection Failure File corruption may occur while reading or writing Marvelous Designer files on external storage such as USB stick or portable hard disk. Although these are convenient, in reality, physical detection failures and connection failures are relatively frequent. When transferring files between an external device and your PC, it often appears that the file-transfer has been complete, but in reality, the all data has not been completely transferred. To check whether the file was completely transferred, simply compare the file size. In summary, allow plenty of time when exchanging files with external storage devices. Case7 Network Drive or Cloud Sync Failure If you use a NAS and various Internet cloud sync services, Marvelous Designer files may be corrupted during file transfer over the network. Additionally, cloud sync services may have problems that removing or damaging files on the local computer during the sync process. If you use a cloud sync service, set it to sync only specific folders, excluding folders and directories referenced by the Marvelous Designer. For example, disable syncing your Desktop and Documents folders. Read More 1 For example, the size of the zprj and zpac files, including Marvelous Designer basic t-shirt and basic avatar, is approximately 20MB. If your files are smaller than expected, it means the internal data may be corrupted. If your project file is less than 1MB in size, it cannot be recovered because all clothing data inside the file has been lost. 2 When recording animations of flashy, heavy garments, the project file size will be very large, and this animation recording data may be fragile in some user scenarios. If you are recording a long animation, dividing the entire scene into sections as shown below will help prevent file corruption. File Recovery If you would like to recover your file, please send us your problem file as is via Contact Us.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
Content: Objective Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. Location Object Browser Fabric Property Editor Physical Property Detail Buckling Stiffness-Weft/Warp

Title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
Content: Objective Import a file's Geometry, Material, Joint, and Camera Animation information in the FBX file format (ver2.2.0). Location Import FBX Main Menu File Import FBX Export FBX Main Menu File Export FBX Operation Import FBX Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import FBX The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Import FBX window appears. Select the settings and click OK. The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Load Type Open All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported FBX file only. Add Add a FBX file, keeping the existing objects. Auto Create Fitting Suit For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Object Type Avatar Import a FBX file as an Avatar type. - Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim Import a FBX file as a Trim type. - The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. - Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. - Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. - Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scene &amp Props Import FBX file in Scene &amp Props format. - You can use the Collision menu in the property window. Object Camera Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported Joint Animation Toggles whether the Joint Animation date is imported. Cache Animation (mc) Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. Automatically Add Arrangement Points For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. Scale Input the Specific Value or Choose Measure. Axis Conversion Modifying Object's Axis direction.(ver. 12.2) Translation Align Bottom to Ground When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. Option Move Garment to Start Position Move the garment to the starting frame of the imported motion. Export FBX Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Export FBX The Save File window appears. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click OK. The Export OBJ window appears. Select the settings as needed and click OK. The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. Object Select an Avatar (ver 6.1) Select the avatar to be exported. Note: The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. Select All Avatars (ver. 12.2) - All existing avatars will be exported. Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. Un-Weld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0 (ver2.3.0). Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Note: * When an object is exported as a single object, its texture is exported as a whole even when its sides (front, back, and side) have different textures (ver5.0.0.) Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Note: * The thickness can be exported when Pattern Mesh is Quadrangular (ver2.3.0.) * Each side's texture is exported individually when an object's front, back, side have different textures (ver5.0.0.) Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. Image File Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: File Name_0, File Name_1. Texture Size Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 512 ~ 8192 Pixel Fill Texture Seams Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Animation Joint Animation: Saves the animation data that was originally imported with the FBX file. Cache Animation (MC): Saves the cache data along with the recorded Garment Animation. Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected. Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) File File Type: Select between Binary or Ascii file type. Binary: The file is saved in binary and cannot be opened by users. Ascii: The file is saved as text and can be opened by users. Relative Texture Image File Path: Saves the texture image name without a texture image file path. Texture images are saved in the same folder as the FBX file, for automatic import. Absolute Texture Image File Path: Saves the file path that contained the texture images as the texture file path. If the texture image file path is changed, texture images cannot be imported. Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Note: FBX SDK 2020 version is available. (ver MD10) Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. Import/Export FBX with multiple avatars

Title: Merge
Content: Objective Merge two Patterns in to a single Pattern. Location Pattern Outline Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Sewing Line Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Pattern Outline Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two Pattern outlines which two Patterns are to be merged accordingly. Note: When the Patterns are symmetrically linked, select the Pattern outline of the either Pattern. Right click on the selected Pattern outlines to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Merge. The selected two Patterns are merged based on the selected Pattern outlines. The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines. Sewing Line Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right click on the Sewing Line which the Patterns are merged accordingly. Then, select Merge. The two Patterns sewn with the selected Sewing Line are merged based on the selected Sewing Line. The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines.

Title: [Property] Scale Avatars
Content: Objective Scale an OBJ imported as an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Import an .OBJ as an Avatar. (ver. 10) Import a .FBX as an Avatar. (ver. 2024.0) Select the tool/ menu indicated in Location. Select the Avatar and click the Scale button to resize the Avatar. The scale Gizmo appears. Click and drag the Gizmo's X-axis (red), Y-axis (yellow-green), Z-axis (blue) or the rectangle. The Avatar size is adjusted according to the selected direction. Click the Scale button to complete scaling. The Gizmo is changed to a standard one that is used to move or rotate the Avatar. Note: Scale with specific values in the Property Window after selecting the Avatar.

Title: Project File (*.ZPrj) Open/Save
Content: Objective Compress the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and save it. Note: Files included in Project (*.zprj) files *.avt file, with all Avatar-related data Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar Size, Poses If there are multiple Avatars, they are all saved within the Project file (ver2.3.0). *.zpac file, containing all Garment-related data (3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Materials) *.anm file, if an Animation has been recorded Any 3D environment settings (Wind, Light, Ground, Background Image/Color, Scenes/Props) Simulation options set by the user (ver2.3.0). Location Open Project File Main Menu File Open Project (Ctrl+O) Save/Save Over Main Menu File Save Project (Ctrl+S) Save As Main Menu File Save As Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) New Project (ver. 12.1) Main Menu File New Project (Ctrl+N) Operation Open Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Project (Ctrl+O) The Open File window opens. Select the desired file and click OK to load the file. Note: Double-click the Project file *.zprj or drag and drop it onto the 3D window to open it. Save Over Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save Project (Ctrl+S) The original Project file is overwritten. Save Project File Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) The Open File window opens. Select a location to save the Garment file. Enter the Project name into the File Name tab and press Save to save the file. A Project file *.zprj will be created along with its thumbnail image. New Project (ver. 12.1) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File New Project (Ctrl+N) The existing file will be closed and a new Untitled project file will be created.

Title: Draw Chalk
Content: Objective Draw chalk lines on 3D Garments. Note: The chalk function has been replaced with Line (3D Pattern) from ver3.0.0. Location 3D Toolbar Line (3D Pattern) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Line (3D Pattern) Click on a desired area on a 3D Garment drag to draw a chalk line. The created chalk line is now being applied and displayed on both of 2D/3D windows.

Title: Roll Up (ver. 12.2)
Content: Feature Overview Makes it easier to fold the ends of garments, such as sleeve openings, pants openings, etc. Steps 1. Select an outline of the 2D pattern with the Edit Pattern tool. - Roll Up does not work on outlines contains a sewing relationship to another pattern. - Roll Up might not work on some segment lines as this feature is optimized for sleeve openings and pants openings that creates a tube. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below. - In 2D Window select a segment line, Right Mouse Button click Roll Up 3. The Roll Up dialog box appears. Enter the desired input. Number of Roll Up Set the number of Roll up to 3 times. Distance Enter a minimum of 10mm and a maximum of 200mm as the distance of each roll up Reset While the dialog box is running, reset the applied Roll Up. Returning the garment to its original state. Apply Apply Roll Up based on the input values entered. Close Close the Roll Up dialog box. - Once you enter the Number of Roll Up and Distance, a green circle will be displayed at the end position of the final garment in the 3D Window as a preview. - Roll Up does not apply symmetrically or to instance modifications. End Result Select Close at the bottom of the dialog to exit Roll Up. - If the Particle Distance of the pattern being rolled up is over 10mm, it will be automatically adjusted to 10 for stable simulation.

Title: Internal Polygon/Line
Content: Objective Create Internal Polygons and Lines inside a Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Internal Polygon/Line Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Internal Polygon/Line 2D Toolbar Internal Polygon/Line Click within a Pattern to establish the start point of an Internal Polygon/Line. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand the Internal Polygon/Line. Right click while freehanding the Internal Polygon/Line to access the Create Internal Polygon/Line window. Use Length, Mirror Creation, and Position options to create the Internal Polygon/Line more precisely and conveniently. Option Description Length Length Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) Mirror Creating The Internal Polygon/Line is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis Local Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Position Left Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its left. Right Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its right. Top Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its top. Bottom Set the distance between the Internal Polygon/Line and the Pattern outline on its bottom. To complete an Internal Polygon, click the start point. On the other hand, to complete an Internal Line, double click the last point. Note: Right click inside a Pattern to open the Create Internal Polygon window and type in desired values. An Internal Polygon is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). Click inside a Pattern to create the start point of an Internal Line. Then, drag and right click to open the Create Internal Polygon window. Enter desired values. An Internal Line is created with the designated values (ver2.5.0). Hold down the Ctrl key as creating an Internal Polygon/Line to create curves. Hold down the Shift key to drag the mouse in straight lines or in 45º diagonal lines. Note: Internal Shape Tool Group Note: Mirror Creating

Title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
Content: Objective This function allows easier simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dresses and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is off. In that state, the arrangement order of the patterns gets decided. Location Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer Operation Select a pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with the Select/Move tool. Note: Select patterns in the 2D window, in case of having difficulties when choosing in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer Apply the value by clicking Simulate button. Note: When the layer value is being set, the patterns become highlighted in blue outline. Once the draping in desired order is completed, set the value back to zero ('0') for a more stable simulation. (There is no change in draping even after modifying the value back to zero('0')). If the layer value is zero('0'), but the menu appears in red when all patterns are being selected, it is because there is a variety of values being mixed. Therefore revert the layer value to zero('0') once again.

Title: Library Window
Content: Objective Conveniently manage and open files in the program using the Library Window. Add frequently used folders to the Library to easily open files: drag and drop a file from the registered folder into the 3D Window or with the left mouse button, double click the file. Operation Icon Menus (Top/Bottom) - Library Window Download (ver MD10) Download newly added default files as a whole. Selectively download files from the folder with the "N" sign. Reset Reset registered folders in the Library. Add Folder Add frequently used folders to the Library. Refresh Apply any changes made in the Library such as deleting or adding folders. Select All (Downloadable Item Only) If you activate a checkbox on the top left corner of downloadable items, the 'Select All' button will appear where the Refresh button used to be. A single selection will select the entire downloadable items, and clicking the button again will deselect all. List / Icon Toggle between different views. (ver2.3.0) Search Use Search to locate files quickly and efficiently within the Library.(ver3.0.0) Right Mouse Button Menus - Library Window Click the RMB on the folders at the top or bottom of the Library window to access the menus below. Delete Delete the bookmarked folder. Rename Renaming the bookmark folder. The name of the original folder saved on the computer will not be changed. Show in Explorer (ver. 12.1) Open the explorer window where the bookmarked folder or the selected folder and files are located. Add to Workspace Add the corresponding item to workspace Note: Show or hide Library Window via selecting the arrow icon in the Library. Hover over the desired Project/Garment file thumbnail to preview font, back, and side views(ver2.4.0.) Only Project/Garment files saved in versions above ver2.4.0 can be previewed.

Title: Solidify
Content: Objective Maintain desired draping state per pattern unit. For instance, solidify creases on the back of the knee area of a pair of jeans to maintain its shape while simulating (ver2.5.0). Location 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu Solidify Operation 3D Toolbar Select a 3D Pattern with Select/Move tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu Solidify The selected Pattern is now being solidified. Follow the indicated guideline and adjust the Strength: Click Pattern Property Editor Bond/Skive Solidify Strength The selected Pattern's 3D shape is now being solidified according to the Strength value. Note: The higher the Strength value, the better the sustenance. Note: 3D Statement

Title: STORE tip 3. STORE in software
Content: You can purchase and download items from the Store within Marvelous Designer software. It is a new feature added to version 11 and is available on both Windows and Mac. After running the software, click the STORE tab on the left to use the store! STORE accounts are the same ones that you would use on our website (www.marvelousdesigner.com) for the login. Click Store, Sign in at the top right and sign in. -Check the STORE items on the item list. -Check the detail page of the item. -Check the items in the shopping cart. -Check the items you have. Please click on the STORE introduction video below! If you click the link below, you will be directed to the STORE Manual. Click on the link.

Title: Ellipse
Content: Objective Create ellipse or circle Patterns in the 2D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Operation Create Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Click and drag on the 2D window. A preview of an ellipse appears. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. While creating the Pattern, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). While creating the Pattern, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). Release the mouse when the desired shape is achieved. The ellipse Pattern is created. Create with Specific Values Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Ellipse 2D Toolbar Ellipse Click in the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. Type in the desired values for the options below. Diameter Set the diameter of the circle Pattern. Radius Set the radius of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Link to maintain the width and height ratio. Circumference Set the circumference of the circle Pattern (ver3.2.0). Note: Create Pattern Tool Group

Title: Polygon
Content: Objective Create polygon Patterns in 2D Window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon 2D Toolbar Polygon Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Polygon 2D Toolbar Polygon Click on the 2D window to make the start point. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand a polygon. Right click while freehanding a polygon. The Create Polygon window appears. Length or Mirror Creation options to create polygon more precisely and conveniently. Option Description Length Length Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) Mirror Creation The polygon is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis Local Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. Click again on the start point to complete the polygon. Note: Pressing the keyboards Delete key while setting points to create a pattern cancels the points, starting from the most recent one. Furthermore, pressing the Esc/Ctrl+Z key during creation cancels the entire operation. While making points to create a Pattern, holding down the Ctrl key and setting points turns segment points into Free Curve Points. This creates a polygon Pattern made up of curved lines. Setting a Segment Point while holding down shift reveals a guideline that can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally at a 45 degree angle according to the Segment Point. Note: Create Pattern Tool Group Note: Mirror Creating

Title: Spiral
Content: Objective Create a Spiral pattern in the 2D Pattern Window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Spiral 2D Pattern Window Toolbar Create Pattern Shape Dropdown Menu Spiral Operation Select the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". Click in the 2D Pattern Window. The Create Spiral pop-up Window appears. After setting the options below, click OK. Radius Set the radius at which a spiral pattern rotates. Length Set the length of the Inner/Outer segment of the spiral pattern. (the two values are linked - editing one will automatically adjust the other) Side Set the Inside/Outside width of the spiral pattern's ends. (editing either will automatically adjust the Length values slightly) Offset Adjust the spacing between spirals. The length you enter is the distance from the center of the spiral pattern to the center of the next spiral layer. Direction Set the rotation direction (Clockwise/Counterclockwise) of the spiral pattern. A spiral pattern is created.
